common_name: Dark and Handsome Lenten Rose (Wedding Party Series)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in late winter to early spring while weather stays cool; established clumps bloom earlier in subsequent seasons.

directions: A WEDDING PARTY series Lenten rose bred by Hans Hansen at Walters Gardens, bearing fully double, near-black to black-purple flowers 2.5-3 inches across held above leathery, evergreen foliage. Flowering runs from late winter into mid-spring, continuing for six weeks or more once clumps mature. Site in part to full shade away from hot afternoon sun, and simply trim back tattered old foliage in spring rather than dividing routinely. Tolerant of drought once established and generally untroubled by deer or rabbits.

common_name: Blushing Bridesmaid Lenten Rose (Wedding Party Series)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in late winter to early spring while weather stays cool; established clumps bloom earlier in subsequent seasons.

directions: Part of the WEDDING PARTY series bred by Hans Hansen at Walters Gardens, this Lenten rose opens double white flowers 2-2.5 inches across, veined and edged in raspberry pink in a delicate picotee pattern, over leathery evergreen foliage. Bloom begins in late winter and continues into mid-spring, often lasting six weeks or more on mature plants. Grow in part to full shade in rich, moist, organic soil, though established clumps tolerate sandy or clay ground and brief drought. Trim away last year's foliage in spring rather than dividing, since hellebores resent frequent disturbance.

common_name: Mother of the Bride Lenten Rose (Wedding Party Series)
scientific_name: Helleborus x hybridus 'Mother of the Bride'

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in late winter to early spring while weather stays cool; established clumps bloom earlier in subsequent seasons.

directions: A WEDDING PARTY series selection bred by Hans Hansen at Walters Gardens, producing large, fully double apricot flowers 3 inches across edged with a light pink picotee rim, held above leathery evergreen foliage. Flowering begins in late winter and extends into mid-spring. Plants grow slowly and prefer part to full shade with average to fertile, slightly acidic to slightly alkaline soil, tolerating low water once established. Deer- and rabbit-resistant, with simple spring cleanup of old foliage as the main maintenance task.

common_name: First Dance Lenten Rose (Wedding Party Series)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in late winter to early spring while weather stays cool; established clumps bloom earlier in subsequent seasons.

directions: Bred by Hans Hansen at Walters Gardens as part of the WEDDING PARTY series, 'First Dance' bears double flowers 2-2.5 inches wide in bright to soft yellow with a maroon picotee edge and fine maroon veining, set against dark, leathery evergreen leaves. Bloom opens in late winter and continues into mid-spring, often for six weeks or longer. Site in part to full shade shielded from hot afternoon sun, in average to fertile, neutral to slightly alkaline soil. Vigorous and low-maintenance, it is deer- and rabbit-resistant and needs only a spring trim of old foliage.

common_name: Father of the Bride Lenten Rose (Wedding Party Series)
scientific_name: Helleborus x hybridus 'Father of the Bride'

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in late winter to early spring while weather stays cool; established clumps bloom earlier in subsequent seasons.

directions: A WEDDING PARTY series Lenten rose from Walters Gardens breeder Hans Hansen, carrying large, fully double gold-yellow flowers 2-2.5 inches wide marked with a burgundy center pattern; the blooms face outward to the side rather than nodding straight down, an unusual trait among double hellebores. Flowering spans late winter through mid-spring over evergreen foliage. Grow in part to full shade with moist, organic soil, though plants adapt to sandy or clay ground and tolerate dry spells once established. Slow-growing and low-maintenance, it needs only a spring tidy of last year's leaves.

common_name: Black Tie Affair Lenten Rose (Wedding Party Series)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in late winter to early spring while weather stays cool; established clumps bloom earlier in subsequent seasons.

directions: Bred by Hans Hansen at Walters Gardens for the WEDDING PARTY series, 'Black Tie Affair' opens near-black double flowers 3 inches across with a subtly lighter center, held above dark, leathery evergreen foliage from late winter into mid-spring. Plants grow slowly into a tidy clump, performing best in part to full shade in average to fertile soil with neutral to alkaline pH, and tolerate both drought and salt once established. Low-maintenance and largely pest- and disease-free, it needs only a spring trim of the previous year's leaves to look its best.

common_name: Dashing Groomsmen Lenten Rose (Wedding Party Series)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in late winter to early spring while weather stays cool; established clumps bloom earlier in subsequent seasons.

directions: A WEDDING PARTY series Lenten rose from Hans Hansen's breeding program at Walters Gardens, producing double flowers 3 inches wide in near-black shades ranging from slate gray to dark purple, carried above leathery evergreen foliage. Bloom extends from late winter into mid-spring. It adapts to sandy, clay, or organic soil as long as it sits in part to full shade protected from hot afternoon sun, and tolerates drought once established. Deer- and rabbit-resistant and essentially pest- and disease-free, it asks only for old foliage to be trimmed away in spring.

common_name: Childhood Sweetheart Lenten Rose (Wedding Party Series)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in late winter to early spring while weather stays cool; established clumps bloom earlier in subsequent seasons.

directions: Part of the WEDDING PARTY series bred by Hans Hansen at Walters Gardens, this selection bears double flowers with yellow interior petals heavily veined in red and dark red petal backs, giving a two-toned effect as blooms nod and turn on evergreen plants. Flowering runs from late winter into mid-spring. It performs best in part to full shade with neutral to slightly alkaline soil and tolerates low to average water once established. Low-maintenance and deer- and rabbit-resistant, it needs only a spring trim of the prior season's foliage.
